questions.q: Which of the following descriptions best explains the social and economic fellowship of the Early Church as recorded in Acts 2:44-45?
options: Believers lived independently and only met for worship once a year.
They charged each other money for food and housing to grow the church fund.
They strictly separated the rich believers from the poor believers.
They had all things in common and sold their possessions to share with anyone who had need.
questions.explain: The early Christians practiced a radical form of togetherness: "And all who believed were together and had all things in common. And they were selling their possessions and belongings and distributing the proceeds to all, as any had need."

questions.q: In Acts 5:1-11, Ananias and Sapphira sold a piece of property but kept back some of the proceeds while presenting it as the full amount. What was the severe consequence of lying to the Holy Spirit?
options: They were expelled from Jerusalem permanently.
They were made to serve the apostles as slaves for seven years.
They fell down and died instantly.
questions.explain: Peter rebuked Ananias for lying to the Holy Spirit, and immediately Ananias fell down and breathed his last. About three hours later, his wife Sapphira did the same and suffered the identical fate.

questions.q: What specific internal dispute caused the apostles to recognize the need to select deacons in the early church? (Acts 6:1)
options: A disagreement over whether Gentile converts should be circumcised
The Hellenists (Greek-speaking Jews) murmured that their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution.
Some disciples wanted to appoint a new king for Israel.
A debate arose about where the church should hold its Sunday meetings.
questions.explain: Acts 6:1 explains the root of the murmuring: "Now in these days when the disciples were increasing in number, a complaint by the Hellenists arose against the Hebrews because their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution."

questions.q: When selecting the seven deacons for the daily distribution, the apostles requested men of "good repute" who also possessed what two critical spiritual qualities?
options: Full of the Spirit and of wisdom
Deep knowledge of Roman law and Greek philosophy
questions.explain: The apostles instructed the congregation, "Therefore, brothers, pick out from among you seven men of good repute, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we will appoint to this duty." (Acts 6:3)
